subject.title: [Feature]: Audio file support in read tool (multimodal parity with images)

question: Should OpenClaw make native audio a first-class read-tool and LLM content type, or keep read text/image-only and route audio through transcription/media-understanding workflows?
rationale: The request changes provider payload shape, local-file egress, model capability routing, unsupported-model behavior, and transcript/session representation, so the permanent contract cannot be inferred safely from current code.

options.title: Design shared native-audio contract first
options.body: Settle the typed content block, provider serialization, payload/security limits, session persistence, and fallback behavior before code lands.

options.title: Fold into broader native-audio tracker
options.body: Keep this linked to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/51667 and require that design to explicitly cover local read-tool audio files.

options.title: Keep read text/image-only
options.body: Document audio as a transcription or media-understanding workflow and decline native read-tool audio for now.

recommendation.title: Design shared native-audio contract first
recommendation.body: Settle the typed content block, provider serialization, payload/security limits, session persistence, and fallback behavior before code lands.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest current path history across the read tool, LLM content contract, and media-understanding package boundary.
